assumptions_made.assumption: Marcus Webb's 'no limit' is encoded as a $50,000/month ceiling. Ramp requires a limit amount; $50,000 is Diane's own stated practical equivalent, not a number we chose.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Marcus's real spend can exceed $50k in a month his card declines — the exact outcome Priya warned would get the project renamed. Confirm the ceiling with him before go-live.

assumptions_made.assumption: Marcus Webb (CEO) is mapped to BUSINESS_ADMIN. The config schema's role enum has no BUSINESS_OWNER.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Marcus gets full administrative rights over the instance, which is broader than a pure owner role. If Acme wants him to spend but not administer, downgrade to BUSINESS_USER.

assumptions_made.assumption: Kevin O'Rourke is mapped to GUEST_USER as the most locked-down assignable role.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'he should absolutely not see anything about anyone else's spend'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If GUEST_USER is more restrictive than his job needs he cannot spend on job boards; if less, he sees more than intended. Note his email is an external domain (orourketalent.example).

assumptions_made.assumption: Priya Shetty is mapped to BUSINESS_ADMIN rather than BUSINESS_BOOKKEEPER, because she was named as an instance administrator as well as the person who closes the books.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: BUSINESS_BOOKKEEPER would match 'close the month' more exactly but could not administer users or limits, which Diane explicitly asked for.

assumptions_made.assumption: Sana Qureshi is mapped to IT_ADMIN, which grants people administration without spend-control authority — the exact split requested.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'Sana should not be able to change spend limits though. Just people stuff.'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Acme expects Sana to also issue cards, IT_ADMIN blocks it unless manager permissions are enabled for her direct reports.

assumptions_made.assumption: The $75 receipt threshold is an in-app policy setting and is deliberately omitted from this config rather than encoded anywhere.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: None to card behaviour; the deployment owner sets it in-app during setup. If missed, receipts are not enforced at all.

assumptions_made.assumption: The $500 memo threshold is an in-app policy setting and is deliberately omitted from this config.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'And memo required for anything over five hundred.'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: None to card behaviour; set in-app. If missed, memos are not required and month-end coding gets harder.

assumptions_made.assumption: Roster department values 'sales' and 'Sales' are the same department, normalized to 'Sales'.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If they are genuinely distinct, Fatima Diallo and Ivy Chen land in the wrong department and inherit the wrong program targeting.

assumptions_made.assumption: IT is included as a fifth department, taken from the roster even though the call named only four.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If IT should roll into G&A, Sana sits in a department of one and any future department-targeted program misses her.

assumptions_made.assumption: Han Zhao's monthly limit is taken as $1,200 — the value on the later of his two duplicate roster rows.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: He gets $1,200 rather than the $500 every other engineer gets. Row order is a weak tie-breaker; this is logged as a conflict and needs a human answer.

assumptions_made.assumption: Engineering's request-based access to the travel program is recorded here rather than in the config, because the config schema has no issuance_rules field. The Ramp API does support this.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'Nobody in Engineering by default; they can request.'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If the deployment owner does not set the program's requestable issuance rule for Engineering, engineers cannot request travel cards at all.

assumptions_made.assumption: The config's top-level 'limits' section is emitted in the shape the exercise schema requires; applying it means posting to /developer/v1/funds.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: None to this document. Anyone writing the apply step against a literal /limits path will 404.

assumptions_made.assumption: Renata Flores's 'decent limit' is taken as the roster's $3,000, under the stated rule that the roster wins.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'She should have her own card with a decent limit'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If 'decent' meant more than $3,000 she will hit declines on office spend, which is her daily job.

assumptions_made.assumption: 'Software-ish' is mapped to the single Ramp category 'SaaS / Software' (code 40).
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'And it should decline anything that isn't software-ish.'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Purchases Acme considers software but Ramp categorizes elsewhere — hardware-bundled tools, some marketplaces — will decline on the software card.

assumptions_made.assumption: 'Actual travel categories' is mapped to Airlines, Lodging, Taxi and rideshare, and Restaurants (codes 4, 6, 8, 19).
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'restricted to actual travel categories — airlines, hotels, rideshare, restaurants while traveling'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Restaurants cannot be scoped to 'while traveling' — the category is unconditional, so travel cards will also work at local restaurants. Car rental (code 5) was not named and is excluded; confirm.

assumptions_made.assumption: The travel limit is modelled as one group limit over a named cohort of 11 travellers, which fans out to one fund per person at apply time.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — 'Everyone in Sales, plus Marcus, plus me, plus Tom Reyes in Marketing'
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Acme meant one shared $2,000 pool rather than $2,000 each, total travel exposure is 11x what they expect.

assumptions_made.assumption: A single existing US entity is assumed; the packet never names a legal entity or discusses multiple.
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Acme has more than one legal entity, users are attached to the wrong one and locations would be needed to separate them.

missing_information_flags.question: Sam Whitfield has no Target_Limit_USD_Monthly on the roster. What monthly limit should he get? No limit has been emitted for him, so he currently gets no card.
Jenny Park's manager is listed as dkim@acme.example, who does not appear anywhere in the roster. Who is her actual manager? Her direct_manager_email is emitted as null.
Han Zhao appears twice on the roster with monthly limits of 500 and 1200. Which is correct?
Marcus Webb's $50,000/month ceiling is our encoding of 'no limit'. Does Marcus accept that number?
Physical cards were requested for all of Sales and for travellers, but the packet contains no shipping addresses. Ramp requires a shipping_address per physical card.

Who do the two newest Marketing hires (Aisha Bello, started 2026-05-18; Grant Sokol, started 2026-06-29) report to after the reorg? The roster says Lucy Tran and Tom Reyes respectively; Priya flagged both as possibly stale. Encoded as the roster states, per instruction not to block.
Kevin O'Rourke's email is on an external domain (kevin@orourketalent.example). Is that intended for his Ramp account, or should he have an acme.example address?
The call named four departments for spend; the roster contains a fifth, IT, with one member. Should IT be its own department or roll into G&A?
Is Car rental (Ramp category 5) intended to be in scope for the travel program? It was not named alongside airlines, hotels, rideshare and restaurants.
Go-live is wanted before the September close. Which date is the hard deadline?

conflicts.description: Marcus Webb's spending limit. The roster records a non-numeric 'NO LIMIT'; the call offers $50,000/month as the practical equivalent, and Priya asks for very-high rather than none.
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded $50,000/month. The stated roster-wins rule does not resolve this one: 'NO LIMIT' is not a value Ramp can express at all, so the call's number is the only representable option. Flagged for Marcus's confirmation.

conflicts.description: Han Zhao's monthly limit. The roster contradicts itself — the same email appears on two rows with different limits.
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded $1,200, the later row. The roster-wins rule cannot arbitrate a roster that disagrees with itself, so this is row order only — a weak reason. Blocking flag raised.

conflicts.description: Number of departments. The call names four departments for spend purposes; the roster contains five distinct department values.
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded all five, including IT, under the stated rule that the roster wins where it and the call disagree.

conflicts.description: Reimbursements. Diane states the goal is to eliminate reimbursements, then immediately asks to keep them enabled for edge cases.
conflicts.source_a: discovery_call_01.txt — 'We want to basically kill reimbursements.'
conflicts.source_b: discovery_call_01.txt — 'Keep reimbursements on for edge cases'
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Reimbursements left enabled at the company level; disabled on the Software program specifically, where a card-only rule was explicit ('Nobody buys software on a personal card, period.'). The two statements are a stated direction and a stated exception, not a true contradiction.

conflicts.description: Whether the roster's manager column is authoritative. Diane confirms managers are as listed; Priya immediately qualifies that the two newest Marketing hires may be stale after a reorg.
conflicts.source_a: discovery_call_01.txt — 'And manager approvals — managers are as listed in the roster's manager column?'
conflicts.source_b: discovery_call_01.txt — 'The roster's manager column is right for everyone except possibly the two newest Marketing hires'
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded the roster's manager column as written for all users, per the explicit instruction not to block and not to invent. The two named hires are flagged non-blocking for confirmation.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Three-tier approval chain: under $500 auto-approves, $500-$5,000 to the direct manager, over $5,000 to Diane Marsh personally with no delegation.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: The Developer API has no approval-policy write endpoint. The chain is emitted as desired state in approval_policies but cannot be applied programmatically; it is built in Ramp's in-app approvals workflow builder.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — no approval-policy write endpoint; only /blank-canvas-approvals/* (acts on existing instances) and GET /spend-programs/{id}/workflow-nodes (read-only); zero approval OAuth scopes. support.ramp.com 'Set up your spend approval policies', checked 2026-08-30 — tiered approval chains ARE configurable in Ramp's in-app approvals workflow builder, so this is a UI-only capability rather than a missing one.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Emit the full tier structure as desired state, then hand the deployment owner a UI checklist to build the same chain in Ramp's approvals workflow builder.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Any new software vendor requires Diane's approval regardless of amount, including a $10/month tool.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: The rule is keyed on vendor novelty, not amount. There is no approval write surface, and approval_policies[].tiers[] is keyed only on threshold_usd_cents, so the exercise schema cannot express 'regardless of amount' except as a zero-threshold tier that also catches all other spend on that program.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — no approval write surface; additionally 'new vendor' is not threshold-shaped and approval_policies[].tiers[] is keyed only on threshold_usd_cents.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Record in the audit log as a process control. The deployment owner can approximate it in-app with a low-threshold tier on a dedicated new-vendor spend program, at the cost of catching amount-based traffic too.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A card with no spending ceiling for the CEO.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp requires an interval and a limit amount on every fund; there is no unlimited sentinel. Encoded as a $50,000/month ceiling with an explicit assumption.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — ApiFundSpendingRestrictionsRequestBody requires both 'interval' and 'limit', and limit.amount is a required integer; there is no unlimited sentinel.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Encode a deliberately high ceiling and record the exact number as an assumption with impact_if_wrong. Never emit a high number silently — "no limit" and "$50k/mo" are different promises to the person holding the card.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A single $2,000/month travel limit covering a named cohort of eleven travellers.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: POST /funds takes one user_id, so a group limit is a fan-out to one fund per member rather than a native object. Whether Acme wants $2,000 each or $2,000 shared is not stated and changes total exposure elevenfold.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — POST /funds requires a single user_id, so a group limit fans out to one fund per member; is_shareable with /funds/{id}/members is the nearest shared-pool primitive and has different semantics (one shared pot, not N).
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Emit assigned_to.group as the customer stated it and record in notes whether the intent was per-person (fan out to N funds) or a genuinely shared pot (one is_shareable fund with members). These are different products and the customer's phrasing usually does not distinguish them — ask.

unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: There is no receipt-threshold configuration resource in the Developer API. Correctly omitted from the config and recorded as an assumption instead.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — no receipt-policy configuration resource; /receipts covers receipt objects and ingestion, not thresholds. Receipt rules are an in-app setting.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Deployment owner sets the receipt threshold in-app during setup.

unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: There is no memo-policy or threshold configuration surface. Correctly omitted from the config and recorded as an assumption instead.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — /memos exposes memo objects but no memo-policy or threshold configuration surface; the rule is an in-app setting.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Deployment owner sets the memo threshold in-app during setup.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Kevin O'Rourke must not see anything about anyone else's spend.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp scopes transaction visibility by reporting chain rather than by department, and GUEST_USER is the most restricted assignable role — so this is largely achievable, but there is no API-creatable custom role to guarantee it field by field.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: support.ramp.com 'User roles overview', checked 2026-08-30 — transaction visibility follows the reporting chain, not department labels, and manager permissions are scoped to the manager's own team; that chain is settable via direct_manager_id on POST /users/deferred. Finer scoping (Custom Roles, entity restriction) exists in-app on Ramp Plus but is not API-creatable — openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 shows GET /roles is read-only.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: First model the reporting chain — set direct_manager_id so each person reports to the manager who should see them, and is_manager on that manager. That covers most of the ask natively. The common partial-permission ask, "manage users but not spend limits", is a stock role rather than a gap — see CAP-IT-ADMIN-SCOPE. Only scoping that follows neither reporting lines nor a stock role needs a Custom Role, which is Ramp Plus and in-app. Confirm the customer's plan tier before promising it.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A long-running contractor account for Kevin O'Rourke.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: GUEST_USER accounts are automatically given a scheduled_deactivation_date six months from invite unless explicitly nulled. Kevin is an ongoing fractional recruiter, so his card will stop working mid-engagement if this default is left in place.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — GUEST_USER accounts receive an automatic scheduled_deactivation_date six months from invite unless explicitly nulled; the field is not settable for admins or owners.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: A default with teeth: choosing GUEST_USER for a long-running contractor quietly schedules their deactivation. Flag it whenever GUEST_USER is assigned.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Virtual software card held by IT; physical cards for everyone in Sales and for travellers.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Virtual cards are GET-only in the API — they are issued as a side effect of funds rather than created directly — and physical card creation requires a shipping_address per cardholder, which this packet does not contain.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — POST /cards/physical exists (requires shipping_address and user_id) but virtual cards are GET-only and are issued via funds rather than created directly.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Express the physical/virtual split through permitted_spend_types on the fund and issue_physical_card_if_needed on the program. Physical issuance additionally needs shipping addresses, which packets rarely contain — usually a missing-information flag.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Iterative tuning of the Software and Travel programs after go-live.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Spend programs support GET and POST only; there is no PATCH or DELETE, so a program is effectively immutable once created via the API. This raises the stakes on reviewing the two programs before they are created.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 — /spend-programs has GET and POST only and /spend-programs/{id} is GET-only; there is no PATCH or DELETE, so programs are immutable via the API.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Get programs right the first time, or edit in-app. This raises the stakes on the config review before go-live and is worth saying in the handoff.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Distinct permission levels for a CEO, a VP Finance, a Controller, an office manager, an IT administrator and an external contractor.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Acme's six distinct roles must be mapped onto Ramp's six fixed roles, which carry no seniority or scoping dimension. Each non-obvious mapping is recorded individually in assumptions_made.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: openapi snapshot 2026_08_30 plus support.ramp.com 'User roles overview', checked 2026-08-30 — Ramp exposes six assignable roles with fixed, documented permission sets and no seniority or scoping dimension, so mapping customer titles onto them is a per-person judgement call.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Every non-obvious mapping gets an assumptions_made entry naming the title, the chosen role, and what the person will consequently be able to see or do. Bookkeeper for close-the-books staff, AUDITOR for read-only compliance, GUEST_USER for contractors (see CAP-GUEST-EXPIRY-DEFAULT), IT_ADMIN for identity owners (see CAP-IT-ADMIN-SCOPE), BUSINESS_ADMIN for owners (see DRIFT-ROLE-BUSINESS-OWNER). Never infer a role from seniority alone.
